03What It IsOVERVIEW▶

A Claude skill that turns a short request ("make me a Fusion tool that ...") into a complete, installable Autodesk Fusion add-in. Every tool Swami commissions has the same shape: a non-modal HTML palette that stays open while he works, a dark theme, collapsible sections, a title like ToolName (v1.0.0), a toolbar icon, room for a keyboard shortcut, visible error reporting, a Reset to defaults control, and double-click installers for both platforms.

It covers the palette and packaging layer. The Fusion Python API rules underneath (persistent handler references, full teardown in stop(), document-type awareness, top-level try/except) come from the fusion-addin-scaffold skill, and the installers come from the fusion-addin-installer skill. It starts from Swami's request template, whose three blanks are the add-in name, its location(s) and a description.

Version 1.1.0 (Nov 7, 2026) brought the manifest in line with Autodesk's documented spec (autodeskProduct = Fusion360, a fresh GUID for id) and moved installer building to fusion-addin-installer.

Why it mattersSwami builds many small Fusion tools. A fixed house spec means none of them ships without the version in the title, the reset, the error strip or an installer, and every tool looks and behaves the same in the toolbar.
04What It DoesOVERVIEW▶
  • IntakeAsks only for the three things it can't guess: the add-in name, where the button goes (default DESIGN › Utilities › Add-Ins, several places allowed) and what the tool does. Everything else gets a house default.
  • Add-in CodeWrites ToolName.py from assets/addin_template.py: the versioned title, buttons in one or more panels, the palette lifecycle, the JS↔Python bridge, settings load and save, reset, and teardown.
  • Palette UIWrites palette.html from assets/palette_template.html: the house dark theme (#0d0d0f / #00e5ff) for a 380 px docked panel, collapsible sections closed on first open, an error strip at the top, and a footer with the version and Reset.
  • ManifestWrites ToolName.manifest with autodeskProduct set to Fusion360, a freshly generated GUID as id, the same version as the .py, and runOnStartup on.
  • IconDraws a 16, 32 and 64 px toolbar icon with scripts/make_icons.py. The icon is what makes Fusion offer Change Keyboard Shortcut.
  • Settings and ResetKeeps settings in a per-user JSON file outside the add-in folder, so reinstalling keeps them. Reset restores every option and every bit of UI state, after a confirmation.
  • InstallersAdds install-macos.command, install-windows.cmd and install-windows.ps1, built with the fusion-addin-installer skill.
  • PreflightRuns scripts/preflight.py: compiles the .py, syntax-checks the macOS installer, checks the folder, .py and .manifest names match, finds leftover template placeholders and checks the versions agree. Claude then checks the two manifest fields by hand.
  • DeliveryZips the folder with the zip command (which keeps the installer executable), sends it, and says the version, where the button lands, how to install, and how to set a keyboard shortcut.

08Capabilities and LimitationsSCOPE▶
  • Whole PackageOne request gives a working add-in folder: code, manifest, palette, icons and both installers, checked and zipped.
  • Stays OpenThe palette is non-modal and dockable, so it stays open while you work in Fusion; the button toggles it.
  • Many PlacesOne tool can put its button in several workspaces or panels.
  • Survives ReinstallsSettings and the keyboard shortcut stay when the add-in is reinstalled, and new settings in later versions appear with their defaults.
  • Visible ErrorsPython errors show in the palette's error strip instead of failing silently.
  • Can't Test in FusionClaude can't run Fusion. The code is compiled and checked, but Swami tests it live.
  • No Hotkey BindingThe add-in can't set its own keyboard shortcut; Swami sets it once in Fusion.
  • Panel IDsFusion's workspace and panel IDs aren't fully documented and change between releases. For an uncertain location the skill ships a snippet that lists the live IDs instead of guessing.
  • Not for EverythingNot for one-shot scripts, plain native-dialog add-ins, or API debugging with no HTML UI (use fusion-addin-scaffold), and not for documentation pages (use vibe-dashboard).
  • Unsigned InstallersThe installers are plain scripts, not signed or notarized packages, so Gatekeeper (and possibly SmartScreen) asks once.

11GotchasGOTCHAS▶
  • Names Must MatchThe folder, .py and .manifest must share one name or Fusion won't list the add-in. Renaming later touches about ten files, so the name is asked for first.
  • Version Not BumpedEvery rebuild must bump the version (the VERSION constant and the manifest). An unchanged title after a reinstall makes it impossible to tell whether the new copy loaded.
  • Version Shown at StartupThe version listed in Scripts and Add-Ins is read when Fusion starts, so it can lag until a restart; the palette title is current.
  • Garbage-collected HandlersEvent handlers must be kept in a list, or Fusion drops them and the palette stops responding.
  • Duplicate PaletteA reload that skipped teardown leaves the old palette alive; the code reuses it by ID instead of adding a second.
  • Relative PathA bare palette.html path loads inconsistently; the palette URL is built from the add-in's own folder.
  • Light ScrollbarsWithout color-scheme: dark, scrollbars and form controls render light on Windows.
  • No NetworkThe palette may have no internet, so no Google Fonts or CDN scripts; it uses system fonts.
  • Half a ResetAny new saved value must be added to DEFAULTS in the same edit, or Reset will look like it worked but leave it behind.
  • Lost Executable BitPython's zipfile drops the executable bit and the .command does nothing; the skill zips with the zip command. Recovery: chmod +x install-macos.command.
  • GatekeeperOn a Mac the first double-click may say the file is from an unidentified developer: right-click › Open › Open, once.
  • Windows: Extract FirstRun the installer from an extracted folder, not from inside the zip. If SmartScreen appears, More info › Run anyway (untested).
  • Windows: Execution PolicyDouble-click the .cmd, not the .ps1. Never change the machine's policy with Set-ExecutionPolicy; the .cmd bypasses it for one run.
  • Document SurgeryIf a document change misbehaves when run straight from the palette's message handler, it's moved into a command definition instead.
12Other RequirementsREFERENCE▶
  • FusionAutodesk Fusion installed and run at least once for the current user, on macOS or on Windows 10 or 11.
  • Code ExecutionClaude needs code execution ("Create and edit files") to build, check and zip the add-in.
  • Companion SkillsThe fusion-addin-scaffold and fusion-addin-installer skills installed alongside this one.
  • No Admin RightsThe installers copy into per-user folders, so no administrator password is needed on either platform.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
PaletteFusion UIA panel in Fusion that shows an HTML page; it can float or dock beside the canvas.
Non-modalFusion UIA window that stays open while you keep working in Fusion, unlike a dialog that blocks until closed.
DockableFusion UIAble to attach to the side of the Fusion window; house tools dock right at about 380 px wide.
Add-inFusion APIA Python program Fusion loads with run() and unloads with stop(); it can start with Fusion and add buttons.
AddIns folderFusion APIThe per-user folder Fusion loads add-ins from, still under "Autodesk Fusion 360" on both platforms.
ManifestFusion APIThe JSON file next to the .py that tells Fusion the add-in's id, version, product and platforms.
GUIDFusion APIA globally unique ID; every add-in's manifest id must be its own fresh one.
TeardownFusion APIRemoving every button, the command definition and the palette in stop(), so a reload starts clean.
Event handlerFusion APIAn object Fusion calls when something happens; it must be kept referenced or it is garbage-collected.
Command definitionFusion APIFusion's record of a command, which buttons point to; it carries the icon and tooltip.
JS↔Python bridgeBridgeThe message channel between palette.html and the add-in; every message is a JSON string, in both directions.
Error stripPalette UIA red bar at the top of the palette where Python errors appear.
House specPalette UISwami's fixed set of features every Fusion tool must have.
DEFAULTSSettingsThe dict in the .py that is both the factory settings and the list of every saved value.
Reset to defaultsSettingsThe control that restores DEFAULTS, options and UI state alike, after a confirmation.
PreflightPackagingThe script that checks a built add-in before delivery: compile, installer syntax, names, placeholders and version.
Executable bitPackagingThe file permission that lets a .command run on double-click; Python's zipfile drops it.
GatekeeperPackagingmacOS protection that blocks unsigned downloaded files until you right-click › Open once.
SmartScreenPackagingWindows protection that may warn before running a downloaded file; More info › Run anyway.
Execution policyPackagingThe PowerShell setting that blocks .ps1 files; the .cmd bypasses it for one run only.
Keyboard shortcutFusion UIA hotkey Swami assigns in Fusion; only offered for commands that have an icon and a button.
